## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle Esoteric ritual manual on **Vaiśravaṇa-deva-rāja** 毘沙門天王 (here transliterated in full as *Mahā-Vaiśravaṇa-deva-rāja* — 摩訶吠室囉末那野提婆喝囉闍 = Skt. *Mahā-Vaiśravaṇa-deva-rāja*), translated by the late-Tang monk **Prajñācakra** ([般若斫羯囉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5%E6%96%AB%E7%BE%AF%E5%9B%89) = Zhìhuìlún 智慧輪), the principal transmitter of late-Tang Esoteric Buddhism to the Japanese pilgrim **Enchin** 圓珍 (Tendai *Jimon* lineage).

**Abstract**

The text supplies the dhāraṇī-rite for the **Vaiśravaṇa** cycle — the iconography, mantra (transliterated Sanskrit), mudrā, and ritual sequence. As a late-Tang Esoteric production it represents a strand of Vaiśravaṇa-cult material distinct from the Amoghavajra recensions of the previous century ([KR6j0472](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0472), [KR6j0475](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0475)–[KR6j0478](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0478)) — and it is precisely the kind of mid-ninth-century Esoteric material that Prajñācakra transmitted to Enchin in the **Dàzhōng** 9 (855) consecration at Dàxìngshànsì 大興善寺 in Chángān, and subsequently as part of the *Xīnjīngfǎ* 新經法 sent to him in **Xiántōng** 2 (861). The dating bracket reflects Prajñācakra's documented translation activity at Chángān (847–861, the Dàzhōng and Xiántōng reigns).
